Warrior against warrior—Futawagakari. Four things chiefly decide it, they say: climbing performance, maximum speed, acceleration, turning performance.

Climbing needs no recommendation. At the start, who gets the higher position? That much depends on how well you climb.

After the first clash, turning takes charge. Reverse quickly, take the higher position quickly. The enemy is not reserving it for you.

Maximum speed, one could say, decides the power of that all-important first exchange. Faster means a stronger stroke, and yours arriving before his. Both benefits in one purchase.

From the second exchange onward, acceleration decides the speed. The clash has spent it; acceleration must earn it back.

Now, a unit perfect in all four does not exist. Demand more of one ability and, very often, another pays. No separate arrangement is available.

Enlarge the horo: turning improves, acceleration suffers. Make it thick and strong: maximum speed rises, climbing performance makes the sacrifice.

Four virtues, and they cannot live peacefully in the same house. Give one a larger room and another is sleeping outside. Bhai, all four must come to the battle. Yes, yes, they will come. One will come furious because you gave his bed to turning performance.

Usually there is no escaping this relationship. Every smith struggles for the best possible result inside a frame smaller than his ideal. Ideal is very large. Frame has no intention of accommodating it.

Between two true-forged tsurugi, the smiths' skill may make one superior, but generally not absolutely so. Even the weaker unit will surpass the other in one of those four things. Use that advantage, and some road to reversal always remains.

武者と武者の勝負――双輪懸は主に以下の四要素で
決すると云われる。
　上昇性能、最大速力、加速性能、旋回性能の四つだ。

　上昇性能の重大さは論を俟つまい。
　戦闘開始時における高度優勢の確保はこの能力如何
だ。

　最初の激突後は、旋回性能次第となる。
　迅速に反転できる騎体ほど高度優位を奪いやすい。

　最大速力は、勝負において最も重要な最初の一合の
攻撃力を定めるものといえるだろう。
　速力に勝るとはつまり、敵より強力な一撃を敵より
も先に打ち放てる事を意味するからだ。

　そして加速性能は、二合目以降の速力を左右する。
　激突で減殺された速力の回復は、この性能に懸かる。

　これら四種の能力を全て完璧に備える騎体など存在
しない。
　往々にして、一種の能力の追求は別種の能力の削減
と不可分であるためだ。

　翼甲を拡大すれば旋回性が増し加速性が失われる。
　翼甲を分厚く強固にすれば最大速力は高まるが上昇
性能は犠牲になる。

　一般に、この相関関係からは逃れ得ない。
　鍛治師は誰しも、理想より確実に小さい枠組みの中
で最善を求め足掻いている。

　真打劔冑と真打劔冑の対決であれば、鍛冶師の技量
の差による優劣が顕れるにせよ、大概、それは絶対的
ではない。総合評価で劣る側とて四要素のいずれかで
は勝り、その点を生かして逆転する道は必ずある。

The sensation remained faintly in my right forearm. A stroke that should have brought him down, turned aside with no apparent trouble. Very small effort from him. Very clear impression on me.

Ichizo Sorimachi was a formidable warrior. His swordsmanship made up for his unit's weakness. The man was personally paying the machine's deficit.

His Type 90 Dragoon Armour was a celebrated unit in military history, yes. Still mass-produced. Still a model ten years old. In every respect, the gap between it and Muramasa was enormous—and his talent reduced it to nothing.

Objectively, my ability did not rise beyond the ordinary. Between him and me, the material itself was different.

Chief"Plainly put, the occupation force's task is to make our country a military base. One part of its strategy against Russia."
Chief"For that, Yamato's people must be on its side. Rule only by force, have resistance movements springing up everywhere—then where is the leisure for staring down Russia?"
Chief"So Rokuhara's tyranny is tolerated. Let the people cry for rescue from their brutal ruler. Then the occupation force rises to answer. Perfect script. Hero enters exactly when required."

Chief"Destroy the people's faith in Yamato's own warriors. Completely. No local alternative left."

Standard aerial fighting required him to turn downward, build speed, prepare the next exchange.

Show me a retreat, expect me to rush toward the monster.

Then attack from above as I went down.
That, yes. A trick of that sort would cause this man no difficulty.

en.html:
I followed his climbing shape. Closing the distance took little effort. Fighting gravity continuously, the enemy unit had already spent much of its speed.

Still upward. Pitch pulled higher yet. Not satisfied, apparently.

Speed was precious in aerial combat. He was spending it all on altitude. More height, more height. No limit, no pause, no sufficiency.

Toward the zenith.
Toward that round white palace he could never reach.

What did he intend? Even with me following, no change of plan. Was refusing to give up all that remained in him?

Our speed also was vanishing quickly. But Muramasa had gathered enough energy before climbing; his dragoon had come straight out of the sword clash and gone up. That difference remained. Narrowing, yes. Gone, no.

Soon he would be within striking distance. Turn to fight and I would cut him down before he could prepare himself.

He must know he was in check. Still he climbed.

Moon madness? Had it caught him so thoroughly he had forgotten the battle?
Even that thought came.

　それでいながら、尚も昇ってゆく。
　あまつさえ、<ruby>兜角<rt>ピッチ</rt></ruby>を更に引き上げて。

　速力という空の戦いにあっては得難い代価を湯尽し、
竜騎兵は高度を貪る。
　際限なく。止め処なく。飽き足らず。

　天頂へ。
　届く筈もなき白の円宮を目掛け。

　追尾を受けてなお方針を翻さないのは、ただ諦めの
悪さからか。

　<ruby>当方<rt>こちら</rt></ruby>とて速度はみるみる減殺されている。
　だが勢力を充分に確保してのち上昇に転じた村正と、
太刀打からそのまま上昇に移った竜騎兵との差は厳然。
詰まってはいるものの、優劣は明確に有る。

　打ち間に捕捉するのは時間の問題。
　雪車町が迎撃に転じたとしても、態勢を整える前に
斬り伏せられる。

　王手を掛けられている事に、彼は気付いている筈だ。
　<ruby>然<rt>さ</rt></ruby>りながら翔天を止めない。

　月の狂気に魅入られ、戦いを忘れたのか――
　そんな事さえ思う。

en.html:
Lieutenant Max Immelmann.

One of Germany's proud aces. His extraordinary fighting name rang through the European War of 1914–1918, by the Western calendar.

No von in the name. That told the story: dragoon corps, yes; knightly birth, no. No inherited true-forged tsurugi, no Blood Crus. Khandaan ka locker kholo, ancestral miracle nikalo—this convenient equipment policy was not available to him.

For an ace of that age, a highly unusual arrangement. In the early Western 1900s—the middle of Yamato's national-calendar 2500s—mass-produced tsurugi had only recently appeared. Compared with today's models, their performance was very low.

His beloved Fokker E.III was no exception. Wire-braced monoplane, the age's best technology poured into it. Still the gap to a true-forged tsurugi refused to close. Best technology had come; equality had not come with it. The engineer had brought his whole brain. The enemy's great-grandfather had brought something worse.

The aces decorating those battlefields were knights of distinguished old houses, wearing the finest inherited armour. Against them, one cavalry officer called Immelmann. In machine performance, the distance was enormous. No doubt about that.

His posting made the situation worse. Northern France: many enemy knights, almost none on his own side. Most of his country's knights had gone to the Russian front.

On his side, fresh and weaker dragoons, himself included. Opposite, old and powerful Crusaders. Forget glory; remaining alive must have been difficult enough. Pehle zinda raho. First survive, then we shall discuss how splendidly you are doing.

What made him an ace there was something from his boyhood. An encounter with a foreigner.

After the Tokugawa era ended, Yamato absorbed Western culture eagerly, almost in reaction to the previous age's relative closure. Learn this, learn that, learn everything. In military organisation, particularly, it copied Prussia—Germany.

The Prussian army was widely considered Europe's strongest. Military exchange missions went again and again, hungry for technical knowledge.

Among those who went was Junzou Sasaki, sixteenth head of Ono-ha Itto-ryu.

He met the boy Immelmann by chance and taught him swordsmanship. Saw the extraordinary talent, and then taught the secret arts also. Arre, secret is written on the thing. That word has some work to do, surely? Careless? Generous? Whichever word one preferred, apparently, eccentricity was not in short supply.

Back home, people accused him of selling the nation's culture. His reply finished the discussion.

Learn only, never teach? That is stealing wisdom. I learned from the German army; in return, I taught the boy.

Hisab barabar. Account balanced. The people guarding the nation's culture had perhaps hoped for a less inconvenient answer.

Thus Immelmann received Itto-ryu's deepest secrets. Even Sasaki probably never expected him to use them.

The five teachings had been passed down without interruption, yes. But since the founder, their difficulty had defeated every practitioner. Technique had become information. A formality proving full transmission. Knowledge fully inherited; use not available. We know everything, beta. Doing it is a separate department, presently closed.

Then, on the Northern France front, driven to the limit and pursued by a powerful knight, Max Immelmann struggled against approaching death—and brought one secret sword back to life.

Garuda-King Sword.
From vertical flight, reverse and attack downward.
A sword that turns the brink of death into victory over an overwhelmingly stronger enemy.

マックス・インメルマン中尉。
　外暦一九一四年から一九一八年にわたって戦われた
欧州戦争において、比類なき勇名を鳴り響かせた<ruby>独逸<rt>ドイツ</rt></ruby>
の誇る<ruby>撃墜王<rt>エース</rt></ruby>の一人である。

　その名に〝<ruby>侯<rt>フォン</rt></ruby>〟の一語が無い事からも明らかな通り、
彼は竜騎兵団に属してはいたものの、騎士階級の出身
ではなかった。
　<ruby>真打劔冑<rt>ブラッドクルス</rt></ruby>の継承者ではなかったのである。

　この時代の撃墜王としては異例と云わねばならない。
　外暦一九〇〇年代初頭（国紀二五〇〇年代中盤）は
まだ数打劔冑が開発されて間もない頃であり、現在に
比べれば性能は著しく低いレベルに留まっていた。

　彼が愛騎としたフォッカーＥ３とてもそうだ。
　張線支持を採用した単翼騎――当時代の技術の粋が
凝らされた騎体ではあったが、真打劔冑との性能差を
埋めるものでは到底ない。

　その頃、戦場に華を添えた各国の撃墜王――由緒正
しい名門の騎士であり最高の劔冑を継承していた人々
――と、一介の騎兵将校インメルマンとの間に、騎体
性能の点で巨大な隔絶があったことは確実である。

　しかも、彼の配属された北フランス戦線は敵に正規
の騎士が多く、対して味方の騎士は大半が対露戦線に
派遣されていたためほとんど皆無という、実に苛酷を
極める状況下にあった。

　味方は彼を含めて新弱の<ruby>竜騎兵<rt>ドラグーン</rt></ruby>ばかり。
　敵方は古強の<ruby>騎士<rt>クルセイダー</rt></ruby>が居並ぶ。
　……武功を掲げるどころか、生き残るだけでも至難
であったに違いない。

　その死線にあってインメルマンを撃墜王たらしめた
のは、少年期に出会った異国人との体験だった。

　徳川時代の幕引き後、大和はやや閉鎖的であった前
時代の反動のように西洋文化を多く取り入れ、何それ
となく学んだが、軍事編制においてはプロイセン――
ドイツに倣う所が非常に多かった。

　プロイセン軍こそ欧州最精強と見る向きが強かった
ためである。
　幾度となく軍事交流団が派遣され、貪欲に技術知識
を求めた。

　そうして、ドイツに渡った男の一人に……

　小野派一刀流一六代宗家、<ruby>笹木純蔵<rt>ささきじゅんぞう</rt></ruby>がいたのだ。

　彼はふとした事から知り合ったインメルマン少年に、
一刀流剣術を手解きし、その才の尋常ならざるを知る
や、奥義の伝授まで行った。……軽々しいというか、
気前が良いというか、いささか変人だったようである。

　だが彼は帰国の後、国粋の文化を売ったとしてこの
行為に批判を浴びると、こう応えて一蹴した。
　――学ぶのみで教えぬ者は、即ち知恵の盗人である。
自分はドイツ軍に学び、返礼として少年に教えたのだ。

　かくしてインメルマンは一刀流の秘奥を拝受したの
だが、教えた笹木にして彼がその秘技を活用できるだ
ろうとまでは考えていなかったに違いない。

　一刀流五箇の秘伝は絶えず伝えられてきてこそいた
ものの、余りの難解さに使い得た者は始祖以来ついに
なく、技術ではなく単なる知識になり果てていた。
　免許皆伝を示す一種の形式に過ぎなかったのである。

　だが、北仏戦線の極限状況にあって――
　敵の剛強な騎士に追われたマックス・インメルマン
は、差し迫る死に抗う渦中で遂に、秘剣の一つを蘇生
させるに至ったのだ。

　金翅鳥王剣。
　垂直騎航からの反転落下攻撃。
　自己より圧倒的に優る敵を討つ、起死回生の剣。

の騎士を空から墜として敵味方を瞠目させた。
　彼と彼の技は同一視され、その名は欧州を席巻し、
悪魔的な恐怖と戦神的な畏怖の的となった。

　一九一六年に戦死するまで、生涯の撃墜数は一七騎。
　全てがフランスの名だたる騎士である。

　現在なおその名は語り継がれ、知らぬ者とていない。
　最強、無敵、魔剣、神技――彼の死と共に消え失せ
た、戦場そらの幻影まぼろしを示すものとして、諸国の軍人そして
歴史書はその名をいつまでも叫び続ける。

This man—

Coming down: the Immelmann Turn, the Garuda-King Sword. A death stroke without equal.

Falling against climbing. The energy difference was overwhelmingly against me.

What could meet it?
What—

Even this unexpected resistance had not disturbed Sorimachi's sword. His certainty of victory probably had not moved either.

A technique worth trusting, certainly. The art of destroying a warrior, perfected until it approached a nightmare.

To oppose that fantasy, another fantasy was required.

—Helmet Splitter.

A famous impossible story. A flesh-and-blood man, one sword, cleaving steel armour and helmet clean in two.

Not something that could happen. A dream with no address in reality.

However great the master, however fine the sword, a cut a few inches into the crown of a helmet was the limit. Usually, that much was called helmet splitting. Cleanly in half? Dream inside dream inside dream.

But suppose.
Suppose that dream became real.

Such a stroke would go beyond physical law. Some strength of will, some technique trained and trained until it went mad, would have to produce it.

If such a thing existed—
